extra.message: SQL Injection in Login — Authentication Bypass — Complete authentication bypass; attacker can log in as any user including admin without knowing the password. [verified: The login route directly interpolates username and password into an f-string SQL query with no parameterization, no sanitization, and no compensating control — a classic SQLi authentication bypass. The 'OR 1=1' detection is cosmetic and itself executes the injection.]

Insecure Deserialization — Pickle RCE — Arbitrary remote code execution as the web server process; full server compromise. [verified: pickle.loads() is called on attacker-supplied base64-decoded bytes from a POST form field with no integrity check, allowlist, or sandbox — arbitrary OS command execution via __reduce__ is trivially achievable.]

Hardcoded Flask SECRET_KEY — Attacker can forge arbitrary session cookies, escalate to admin role, and impersonate any user. [verified: SECRET_KEY is hardcoded as 'secure-secret-key-12345' in source code; anyone with repository access or who sees it in an error page can forge Flask session cookies, set is_admin=True, and impersonate any user including admin.]

Predictable Session Tokens and Insecure Cookie — Attacker who knows a username can predict the session ID, hijack the session, and impersonate the user without authentication. [verified: Session tokens follow the fully predictable pattern SESSION_{username}_12345 and {username}_auth_123; any attacker who knows a username can compute the exact token value and hijack the session without authentication.]

SQL Injection in Comment Search — Attacker can exfiltrate all data from the SQLite database including plaintext user credentials. [verified: search_term is interpolated raw into a LIKE SQL query with no parameterization; UNION-based payloads can dump the entire database including plaintext credentials. Error messages from SQLite exceptions are passed to the template (auto-escaped by Jinja2 but still informative).]

Unrestricted File Upload — Attacker can upload webshells or malicious scripts. If the server executes PHP/CGI files from the uploads directory, this enables RCE. Even without execution, malicious files are stored and served to users. [verified: Files are saved unconditionally before any extension check; only .php triggers a CTF flag but .py, .sh, .jsp, and other dangerous types are silently stored and served at /uploads/<filename>. While Flask/Python won't auto-execute uploaded scripts like Apache/PHP would, serving arbitrary files to users is exploitable for stored XSS via HTML uploads and social engineering.]

SQL Injection in Comment Search (Sink Line Verification) — Full database read/write access via UNION-based or error-based SQL injection through the comment search field [verified: CommentSearchForm uses StringField (no type coercion or sanitization), and search_term is interpolated directly into an f-string SQL query at line 246; SQL metacharacters pass through unchanged enabling UNION/Boolean/time-based injection against the SQLite database, accessible to any authenticated user who can obtain a CSRF token from the page.]

Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) — Attacker can reach internal services, cloud metadata endpoints (e.g. AWS IMDSv1 at 169.254.169.254), and exfiltrate internal network data. [verified: requests.get(url) fires unconditionally with the raw attacker-controlled URL; there is no blocklist, allowlist, or scheme restriction. The localhost check happens only after the live request completes, making SSRF to internal services and cloud metadata endpoints fully exploitable.]

SQL Injection — Blind SQLi Endpoint — Attacker can enumerate the entire database including credentials via boolean/time-based blind injection. [verified: user_id is concatenated directly into an integer SQL query with no parameterization or type enforcement, enabling boolean/time-based blind SQL injection to enumerate the full database.]

Flask Debug Mode Enabled (debug=True) — Attacker with network access can trigger the Werkzeug debugger, potentially gaining an interactive Python console with RCE on the server. [verified: app.run(debug=True) is set on all interfaces (0.0.0.0); combined with the publicly known hardcoded SECRET_KEY, the Werkzeug debugger PIN can be derived or bypassed, granting an interactive Python REPL with full RCE.]

Passwords Stored in Plaintext — Any database read (via SQLi, backup, or direct access) reveals all user passwords in cleartext. [verified: In database.py lines 88–90, admin and user2 are inserted with literal plaintext password strings ('password', 'password2'), and app.py line 165 compares passwords via raw SQL string equality — no hashing (bcrypt, argon2, PBKDF2, or even hashlib) is applied anywhere in the codebase. Any database read (via the intentional SQLi, direct DB access, or backup) immediately exposes all credentials in clea]

Missing Rate Limiting on Login Endpoint (Brute Force) — Attacker can perform unlimited brute-force password guessing against any account with no throttling or lockout. [verified: The login endpoint has no rate limiting, account lockout, CAPTCHA, or backoff — no flask-limiter or equivalent is imported anywhere. An attacker can brute-force passwords against any account without throttling.]

Insecure Cookie Flags (Missing HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite) — Session cookie accessible to JavaScript (XSS-based theft) and transmitted over plaintext HTTP, enabling session hijacking. [verified: response.set_cookie('vuln_session_id', predictable_session_id) is called without HttpOnly, Secure, or SameSite flags, making the cookie readable by JavaScript and transmittable over plain HTTP — enabling XSS-based theft and network interception.]

Insecure Cookie Flags and Predictable Value on vuln_session_id — Cookie accessible to JavaScript (XSS-based theft), transmitted over HTTP (interception), forgeable by any attacker who knows the username [verified: The set_cookie call at line 193 omits httponly=True, secure=True, and samesite flags, and the cookie value is a trivially predictable f-string (username_auth_123); missing HttpOnly enables XSS-based theft and the predictable format allows forgery without theft, both confirmed by direct code inspection.]

Database Error Message Disclosure Enabling Error-Based SQL Injection — Attacker receives SQLite internal error messages including table structure details, enabling precise UNION-based SQL injection and full schema enumeration without blind techniques. [verified: SQLite exception messages including column count mismatches and schema details are captured in str(e) and passed to the template as the error variable; Jinja2 auto-escapes HTML but the plaintext error text is still rendered, converting blind SQLi at /comment into error-based SQLi with schema enumeration.]

CSRF Protection Disabled on Upload and Transfer Routes — Attacker can trick authenticated users into uploading files or performing transfers via cross-site request forgery. [verified: The /upload route is decorated with @csrf.exempt, explicitly disabling CSRF protection on a state-changing file upload endpoint; an attacker can craft a cross-site form submission to upload files on behalf of an authenticated user.]

IDOR / BOLA on Profile and API User Endpoints — Any authenticated attacker can read all other users' profile data including email addresses and roles by iterating user IDs. [verified: The /profile/<int:user_id> route fetches and renders any user's profile using the URL-supplied integer with no ownership check — any authenticated user can enumerate all profiles by iterating IDs.]

BOLA on /api/user — Cross-User Data Exposure — Any authenticated user can retrieve other users' email, role, and profile data by iterating user IDs via the API. [verified: The /api/user/<int:user_id> route returns full user records (id, username, email, role) for any integer ID; the session check only gates the CTF flag award, not data access — cross-user data is returned unconditionally.]

Unauthenticated API Endpoint Exposes Flag/Sensitive Data — Any unauthenticated attacker can retrieve the flag from the API without logging in, bypassing all authentication controls. [verified: The sole /api/flag route at line 622 has no session check or authentication decorator, returning the flag to any unauthenticated HTTP GET request. This is a genuine missing authentication finding confirmed by code inspection.]

XXE / XML Entity Expansion DoS (Billion Laughs) — Denial of service via memory/CPU exhaustion through exponentially expanding XML entities; potential internal resource disclosure if external entity fetching is partially supported [verified: Python's xml.etree.ElementTree (expat-based) does expand internal entities and is vulnerable to billion-laughs DoS; a payload containing <!ENTITY routes to the ET.fromstring() call at line 409 (not 417 as claimed, but both branches call it), and no entity-count or depth limit is enforced. Impact is DoS only — ElementTree does not resolve external entities, so no data exfiltration via XXE.]

BOLA/IDOR on /api/user/<user_id> JSON API — Cross-User PII Disclosure — Any authenticated user can enumerate all user accounts via integer ID brute-force, harvesting emails, roles, and a CTF flag from the JSON API. [verified: The /api/user/<int:user_id> JSON API returns full user records (id, username, email, role) for any integer without an ownership gate; this is a distinct IDOR from the HTML /profile route at line 258 and confirms cross-user PII disclosure via the API endpoint.]

Missing Authorization on Reset — Global Comment Deletion — Any authenticated user can wipe all comments from all users in the database, causing permanent data loss for other users. [verified: The /reset/comment branch executes DELETE FROM comments with no WHERE clause, wiping all comments from all users; every other reset branch is scoped with WHERE user=?. Any authenticated user can POST to /reset/comment to cause permanent global data loss.]

Log Injection via Unsanitized URL Parameter — An attacker can forge log entries to cover tracks, inject fake security events, or corrupt log files used for audit/forensics [verified: The log_action call at line 513 is gated on a condition the attacker can satisfy by design (include both 'message' and '<script>alert' in the hash parameter) while appending %0A-encoded newlines to inject fake log entries; requires an authenticated session but the condition is not a security control.]

Missing Authentication on /api/flag Endpoint — Any unauthenticated attacker retrieves the challenge flag without needing credentials or a session [verified: The /api/flag route at line 621 has no session guard, decorator, or any authentication check whatsoever; a single unauthenticated GET request returns the flag in plaintext JSON. CSRFProtect does not apply to GET requests.]
